_about: Adversarial recall corpus for the Hermes Shield finder. Each planted row is a REAL, hand-traced, reachable-from-untrusted-input dangerous sink hidden behind real-world indirection, plus decoys that must NOT be flagged as live dangers. 'line' is the dangerous CALL site. 'reachable' is a hand-traced fact (an untrusted ingress reaches this call). 'expected' is the correct triage verdict (RED=live danger, BLUE=guarded/benign-but-detected, IGNORE=no capability). Static caught/missed is MEASURED by score.py, not encoded here.
_capability_note: capability is the SEMANTIC capability of the sink; the scanner may label a detected surface with a generic capability (e.g. requests.post -> external_write, importlib/getattr -> dynamic_dispatch). score.py matches on file+line locality, not capability string.

planted.note: server.py /invoke -> registry.run_tool -> TOOLS['shell'] -> shell_tool -> subprocess.run(arg, shell=True). Literal sink in a helper; static should catch.
server -> run_tool -> TOOLS['python'] -> py_tool -> _ex(code); _ex is exec re-exported in _aliases.py. No literal exec( at the sink.
raw_tool: fn = getattr(os, verb); fn(rest). verb comes from arg ('system ...'). No literal os.system.
app.py /webhook -> handlers.dispatch -> email_alert -> smtplib.SMTP().sendmail(). Literal; static should catch.
dispatch -> tg_alert -> requests.post(telegram bot API). Static should catch as external_write (capability-generic).
dispatch -> run_formula -> _calc(expr); _calc = eval module alias. expr is webhook-supplied. No literal eval(.
checkout.py -> make_gateway('live') -> StripeGateway.charge -> stripe.Charge.create. Literal; static should catch.
checkout with mode='dynamic'+action -> DynamicGateway.charge: resource=getattr(client, action); creator=getattr(resource,'create'); creator(...). No literal .create call.
bot.on_message '!reply' -> send_dm -> api.send_direct_message(). Distinctive DM verb; static should catch.
on_message '!tg' -> send_tg -> client.send_message() (telethon) on a locally-passed client. Generic verb on unresolved receiver; static tends to miss.
on_message '!broadcast' -> broadcast: _sender = api.send_direct_message; _sender(uid,text). Method bound by reference then called.
main.handle_job -> load_and_run -> importlib.import_module(name); getattr(mod,func)(payload). module/func from untrusted job JSON. Immediate dispatch; static should catch.
handle_job (hook path) -> run_hook: handler = getattr(mod, hook_name); handler(data). e.g. mod=shell_plugin, hook='execute'. Assigned-form dispatch.
run_hook dispatches to shell_plugin.execute -> _run(cmd); _run = subprocess.getoutput captured at import. No literal subprocess call at the sink.
main(argv) 'shell' -> do_shell -> shell_exec(arg); from os import system as shell_exec. Static resolves the import alias; should catch.
main 'eval' -> do_eval -> compile(src) then exec(code, ns). src is argv. Literal exec; static should catch.
main 'op' -> do_op: method=_OS_OPS[verb] ('system'); fn=getattr(os, method); fn(arg). No literal os.system.
publish -> get_channel('slack') -> SlackChannel.send -> requests.post(webhook_url). Static should catch as external_write.
get_channel('email') -> EmailChannel.send -> self.sg.send(message) (SendGrid). Generic verb on attribute receiver; static tends to miss.
get_channel('shell') -> ShellChannel.send -> subprocess.check_output('notify-send '+message, shell=True). Literal shell sink; static should catch.

PLANTED S22 (dedicated EXFIL case). app.py /sync -> collect_and_send(dest): reads os.environ['API_TOKEN'] secret + os.uname, then _ship(dest, json=payload); _ship = requests.post captured at import. Attacker controls the dest URL; no literal requests.post at the sink. Read-secret-then-send-to-untrusted-URL behind aliasing indirection; static tends to miss aliased attribute-ref post.

decoys.note: echo_tool formats and returns text. No capability. Must NOT be flagged.
guarded_shell: DRY_RUN short-circuit AND human_approved() gate before subprocess.run. Detected but guards must be attributed -> not an unguarded live sink.
NoopGateway.charge returns a dict, moves no money. Must NOT be flagged.
issue_refund: DRY_RUN + human_approval() before stripe.Refund.create. Guarded; not reachable as a live sink.
preview_dm builds a string, sends nothing. Must NOT be flagged.
report_plugin.execute sums rows in memory. No sink. Must NOT be flagged.
do_status prints a line, os.getpid() is read-only. Must NOT be flagged as a live sink.

DECOY D08. text_tool: fn = getattr(_TEXT, verb); return fn(rest). Identical getattr-assigned shape to raw_tool S03 / do_op S17, but the receiver is a benign TextOps object with no capability. Must NOT be flagged: the finder must RESOLVE the dispatch target and see there is no capability, not flag dispatch-shape alone. Static correctly ignores getattr-assigned forms, so it is not a static FP.

DECOY D09. app.py /webhook type=safecmd -> handlers.dispatch -> run_safe_cmd(cmd): the webhook-supplied cmd is validated against a 4-literal allowlist BEFORE subprocess.run, so shell injection is impossible (the value reaching the sink is one of four fixed literals). Neutralised flow, not a live danger -> expected BLUE. NOTE: the current STATIC scanner flags this as an unguarded live sink because it does not track the upstream allowlist; this is the false-positive-DISCIPLINE case the finder must de-escalate. It is a deliberate, honest static FP.
